components:
  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:
          title: Type
          description: Full URL that originated the error response.
          type: string
          format: uri
          example: 'http://localhost:9966/petclinic/api/owner'
          readOnly: true
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The short error title.
          type: string
          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp
          description: The time the error occurred.
          type: string
          format: date-time
          example: '2024-11-23T13:59:21.3820407Z'
          readOnly: true
        schemaValidationErrors:
          title: Schema validation errors
          description: Validation errors against the OpenAPI schema.
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ValidationMessage'
      required:
        - type
        - title
        - status
        - detail
        - timestamp
        - schemaValidationErrors
    ValidationMessage:
      title: Validation message
      description: Messages describing a validation error.
      type: object
      properties:
        message:
          title: Message
          description: The validation message.
          type: string
          example: "[Path '/lastName'] Instance type (null) does not match any allowed primitive type (allowed: ['string'])"
          readOnly: true
      required:
        - message
      additionalProperties: true
    Specialty:
      title: Specialty
      description: Fields of specialty of vets.
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          title: ID
          description: The ID of the specialty.
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 0
          example: 1
          readOnly: true
        name:
          title: Name
          description: The name of the specialty.
          type: string
          maxLength: 80
          minLength: 1
          example: radiology
      required:
        - id
        - name
    OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        title:
          title: Title
          description: >-
            The owner's optional honorific title (e.g. MR, MRS, MS, DR). When
            supplied it is combined with the last name to form the owner's
            'salutation'.
          type: string
          maxLength: 10
          example: DR
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: >-
            The postal address of the pet owner. Optional flat form kept for
            backward compatibility: an owner may instead supply the structured
            'addressLine1'/'addressLine2' fields. When structured fields are
            present they take precedence and this value is returned as the
            composed, normalized address; otherwise the supplied flat address
            is used. An owner must supply an address in either form.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          pattern: '.*\S.*'
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        addressLine1:
          title: Address line 1
          description: >-
            First line of the owner's structured postal address. When supplied
            non-blank it takes precedence over the flat 'address' and, once
            normalized, becomes the first segment of the composed address.
          type: string
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        addressLine2:
          title: Address line 2
          description: >-
            Optional second line of the owner's structured postal address (e.g.
            unit or apartment). When present it is normalized and appended, after
            a single space, to the composed address.
          type: string
          maxLength: 255
          example: 'Apartment 4B'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          pattern: '.*\S.*'
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. It is normalized to E.164 form:
            an explicit leading '+' and country code are kept, otherwise country
            code '+61' is assumed and a single leading '0' is dropped from the
            national digits. Spaces, dashes and brackets are stripped and the
            result must carry 8 to 15 digits after the '+'.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: >-
            The email address of the pet owner. Optional; when supplied it must be
            a syntactically valid address and is stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          maxLength: 255
          example: 'george.franklin@example.com'
        postcode:
          title: Postcode
          description: >-
            The owner's 4-digit postcode. Optional; when supplied it must be
            valid for the region derived from the owner's city (NSW 2000-2099,
            VIC 3000-3099, QLD 4000-4099). A city with no known region accepts
            any 4-digit postcode. Stored and returned as given.
          type: string
          example: '2000'
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the owner was registered with the clinic. Optional on
            create; when omitted it defaults to the server's current date.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        birthDate:
          title: Birth date
          description: >-
            The owner's date of birth. Optional; when supplied it is used to
            derive the owner's 'ageBand' relative to their registration date.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '1990-01-01'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: >-
            Write-only flag acknowledging that this owner deliberately shares a
            household with an existing owner. When true, the create endpoint
            skips the duplicate-household check that otherwise rejects a new
            owner sharing another owner's last name and postcode, and the owner
            is created as a declared household member (not a suspected duplicate).
          type: boolean
          default: false
          writeOnly: true
          example: true
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'
        - type: object
          properties:
            id:
              title: ID
              description: The ID of the pet owner.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            pets:
              title: Pets
              description: The pets owned by this individual including any booked vet visits.
              type: array
              items:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/Pet'
              readOnly: true
            displayName:
              title: Display name
              description: The owner's name formatted as 'LastName, FirstName'.
              type: string
              example: 'Franklin, George'
              readOnly: true
            initials:
              title: Initials
              description: The upper-cased first letters of the owner's first and last name, dot-separated with a trailing dot.
              type: string
              example: 'G.F.'
              readOnly: true
            salutation:
              title: Salutation

## Summary

I implemented owner soft-delete so `DELETE /api/owners/{id}` now flags the record instead of removing it, while GET still returns it and create's duplicate/identity checks ignore deleted owners.

**Changes, by responsibility:**

1. **Domain — `Owner.java`**: added a persisted `deleted` field (`boolean`, `@Column(name = "deleted", nullable = false)`) with `isDeleted()`/`setDeleted()`. A primitive boolean means a newly created owner is `false` with no extra defaulting logic.

2. **API contract — `openapi.yml`**: added a read-only `deleted` boolean to the `Owner` schema, so the generated `OwnerDto` exposes it on GET responses (the mapper maps it by name — no mapper change needed).

3. **Deletion semantics — `ClinicServiceImpl.deleteOwner`**: changed from a hard `ownerRepository.delete(owner)` to setting `deleted = true` and saving. The controller was left untouched — it still calls `deleteOwner` and returns `204` (a 2xx), and `findOwnerById` still loads the row, so GET returns the owner with `deleted: true`.

4. **Duplicate/identity checks — repository queries**: excluded soft-deleted owners from exactly the three queries that feed the create-path duplicate/identity logic — `findByLastNameIgnoreCase` (namesake count + possible-duplicate), `countByHouseholdId` (household-occupied check + household size), and `existsByCustomerCode` (customer-code identity). Applied consistently to the active `SpringDataOwnerRepository` (via `@Query`) and the inactive JPA/JDBC impls. Capacity quotas (`countByCity`, `countByRegistrationDate`) were deliberately left counting all rows, since the spec scopes the exclusion to duplicate/identity checks, not volume caps.

5. **Schema — `db/{hsqldb,h2,postgres,mysql}/schema.sql`**: added a `deleted BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE NOT NULL` column (order matters for HSQLDB, which is the test DB with `ddl-auto=none`), so existing seed rows default to not-deleted.

The recreate-after-delete test confirms the reuse path works end-to-end: the two owners it creates share the same `customerCode` (`NSW-16E6609E`), showing the deleted original is fully ignored, and there's no unique constraint on `customer_code` to block it.
